own_original_text:
Executive Order 12487 of September 14, 1984
Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the  
United States of America, and in accordance with section 2207 of the Deficit  
Reduction Act of 1984 (Public Law 98-369), it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Executive Order No. 12456 of December 30, 1983, as amended, is  
further amended by replacing Schedule 8 attached thereto with the corre­
sponding new Schedule 8 attached hereto.
Sec. 2. The adjustments of rates of pay made by section 1 of this Order are  
effective on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or  
after January 1,1984.

THE WHITE HOUSE,

versions.research_rationale: EO 12487 of September 14, 1984 (official text 49 FR 36493, saved OCR text layer read in full: two sections, signature and new Schedule 8, filing line) replaces Schedule 8 (judicial salaries) of EO 12456 under section 2207 of the Deficit Reduction Act of 1984, effective from the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 1984. EO 12496 of December 28, 1984 (50 FR 211, read in full) section 6 supersedes EO 12456 'as amended' and its section 3(c)/Schedule 7 sets new judicial salaries, so every clause is terminated, but the effective date depends on a pay-period date that the held sources do not fix. The current-law leads (28 U.S.C. 153 and 172 notes) are historical salary notes ('formerly set out as a note under section 5332 of Title 5'), not continuing bases. No first-end date is asserted. Partial claim.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12496 contains no savings clause for EO 12456 as amended; it sets new judicial salaries under its own Schedule 7. Salaries already paid at the 1984 rates (including the retroactive adjustment to the first pay period of 1984) are completed payments, not continuing effects.
